name: DPS
backbones: thin ResNet of ATS (traffic signs); ResNet-18 (billiard balls); ResNet-50 (CUB, NTS-Net setup)
main_result: ResNet-18 + Transformer aggregation: billiard-balls test acc 93.8 with K=10 selected patches (ResNet-18 on the full image 81.6)
notes: [application] Patch selection for high-resolution recognition whose selected patches go to a CNN feature network, so it is not token reduction inside a ViT. A shallow CNN scorer on a downscaled image scores a grid of patches and a perturbed-maximum differentiable Top-K picks K (5 or 10) patches; sigma decays linearly to 0 during training so inference uses hard Top-K. A small Transformer (3 self-attention layers) is only one of the aggregation options (mean, max, Transformer). The whole model is trained end-to-end; no pre-training of the feature network is mentioned for traffic signs (the paper says pre-training could help), so training is taken as scratch; the CUB setup follows NTS-Net with ResNet-50. Only relative speed is given (hard Top-K 3-10% more images/s; full-image CNN 24% longer training); no FLOPs. The name DPS comes from later work (IPS), not from this paper.
evidence: "we formulate patch selection as a ranking problem, where per-patch relevance scores are predicted by a small ConvNet and the Top K scoring patches are selected for downstream processing" (1. Introduction); "To bridge this we linearly decay σ to zero during training" (4.2); "The whole model is trained end-to-end without any adhoc loss to train the selection module" (Figure 2)

name: PS-ViT
main_result: PS-ViT-B/10: top-1 80.6 at 3.1 GFLOPs, 1348.0 img/s (DeiT-S 79.8 at 4.6 GFLOPs, 1018.2 img/s)
notes: [core] Learned token sampling replaces the fixed ViT patch grid, and the sampling number n sets the sequence length (n=10 gives 100 tokens; the default n=14 gives 196, the same as ViT/16 at 224). A ResNet-50 stem gives a feature map; for N=4 iterations a transformer layer predicts sampling offsets and tokens are re-sampled by bilinear interpolation; a ViT module then processes the n x n tokens. Token count is fixed per model. Trained from scratch on ImageNet-1k for 300 epochs with the DeiT recipe. Throughput on one 32GB V100, batch 128. No pruned DeiT-S setting, so the DeiT-S columns are empty; the gain over DeiT comes from both the CNN stem and the sampling.
evidence: "At each iteration, embeddings of the current sampling step are fed into a transformer encoder layer, and a group of sampling offsets is predicted to update the sampling locations for the next step" (Abstract); "The number of sampling points along each spatial dimension n is set as 14 by default" (3.3); "We train our proposed PS-ViT on ImageNet without pretraining on large-scale datasets" (4.1)

name: STViT
main_result: STViT-S: top-1 83.6 at 4.4 GFLOPs, 564 img/s (DeiT-S 79.9 at 4.6 GFLOPs, 922 img/s)
notes: [out-of-scope?] Super tokens only shorten the input of self-attention and are mapped back to all tokens, so every block keeps the full token map (an efficient-attention backbone, not token reduction). Super Token Attention samples m super tokens by one iteration of a soft k-means-like association (each token to its 9 surrounding super tokens), runs MHSA on the super tokens and upsamples with the association map. Grid sizes 8x8 and 4x4 in the first two stages (m=49 at 224) and 1x1 (no sampling) in the last two. Hierarchical hybrid with conv stem, CPE and ConvFFN, trained from scratch for 300 epochs. Throughput on one V100 with batch 16. Also COCO and ADE20K. arXiv only; no peer-reviewed version found (see g12_bib_notes.md).
evidence: "the first samples super tokens from visual tokens via sparse association learning, the second performs self-attention on super tokens, and the last maps them back to the original token space" (Abstract); "For the first two stages, the sampling grid sizes (as shown in Fig. 4(b)) are set to 8 × 8 and 4 × 4, respectively" (3.3); "All our models are trained from scratch for 300 epochs with the input size of 224 × 224" (4.1)

name: STTABT
notes: [core] Token pruning for ViTs and NLP Transformers judged from the abstract only; the full text could not be read. The OpenReview PDF is behind a browser challenge and there is no arXiv version, so schedule, training, backbones and all numbers are ?. Per the abstract, token importance is back-tracked through the attention from the outputs to the inputs; criterion is set to cls-attention (attention statistics) on that basis. The code URL is from the official README (repository linked to the OpenReview forum); the README mentions ViT and LV-ViT-S concrete-masking runs, GLUE tasks and DynamicViT comparison plots, which are not used here.
evidence: "we propose an attention back-tracking method that tracks the importance of each attention in a Transformer architecture from the outputs to the inputs, to preserve the tokens that have a large impact on the final predictions" (Abstract); "We experimentally validate the effectiveness of the method on both NLP and CV benchmarks, using Transformer architectures for both domains" (Abstract)

name: IPS
backbones: ResNet-18 (ImageNet-1k, traffic signs); ResNet-50 BYOL features (CAMELYON16)
main_result: ResNet-50 BYOL features: CAMELYON16 AUC 98.1 with M=5k selected from all patches, 4.7 GB VRAM, 355 ms per training step (batch 16)
notes: [application] Memory-efficient patch selection for megapixel and gigapixel images (traffic signs, megapixel MNIST, CAMELYON16 whole-slide images) with a CNN patch encoder and a cross-attention aggregator, so it is not token reduction inside a ViT. In no-gradient mode IPS scans patches I at a time and keeps the top-M by the cross-attention score of a learnable query token; only the M kept patches are re-embedded with gradients and aggregated. M is fixed per run (2 to 5k). Traffic-sign encoder is an ImageNet ResNet-18 fine-tuned; CAMELYON16 uses features extracted by a BYOL ResNet-50 and trains the aggregator. Runtime is training forward+backward time on one A100 with batch 16; no inference latency.
evidence: "an iterative patch selection module that selects a fixed number of patches and a transformer-based patch aggregation module that combines patch embeddings to compute a global image embedding" (2 Methods); "They both share the cross-attention layer" (2.2); "a ResNet-18 with ImageNet-1k weights is used as encoder for all methods and then finetuned" (4.1)

name: Tri-Level E-ViT
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; Swin-T; Swin-S; PiT; LV-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.9 with 15.7% less training time and 17.0% MACs saving over training (dense 79.8)
notes: [core] Token pruning by [CLS] attention for ViTs trained from scratch, evaluated on ImageNet; token level is one of three sparsity levels (training examples, tokens, attention connections). The TA-Selector before layers 4, 7, 10 keeps the top R_T N tokens by head-averaged [CLS] attention (column sums of attention for Swin), with R_T warmed up from 1.0 by a cosine schedule, then keeps R_A N attention connections per token; no extra parameters. Example level removes unforgettable training images (forgetting counts plus [CLS]-attention variance). Keep ratios 0.9/0.8/0.7 are chosen from per-level sweeps. MACs saving is over the whole training run; inference GFLOPs of the DeiT-S model are not in the main table. Latency only on a Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA (batch 1, 16-bit fixed point). Read the arXiv v1.
evidence: "Evaluate token importance by the [CLS] token and prune the less informative tokens" (Figure 2); "In this work, we aim to prune tokens without introducing additional modules and train ViTs from scratch with original training recipes" (Token-level Sparsity); "we insert our TA-Selector before the 4th, 7th, 10th layer for hierarchical pruning scheme as in (Rao et al. 2021)" (Datasets and Implementation Details)

name: FLIP
backbones: ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16; ViT-L/14; ViT-H/14 (CLIP image encoders)
main_result: ViT-L/16: ImageNet zero-shot 74.3 with 50% masking and unmasked tuning, 32 epochs on LAION-400M (own CLIP reproduction 72.4)
notes: [vlm?] Random patch removal is used only while pre-training CLIP to cut training cost; inference runs on intact images, so the deployed encoder keeps all tokens. 50% or 75% of image patches are dropped at random and the ViT encodes only the visible ones (as in MAE), which allows 2-4x larger batches; an optional unmasked tuning of 0.32 epoch reduces the train-test gap. ViT-L/16 ablation: masking 50% takes 0.50x the wall-clock time and 0.52x the FLOPs of the CLIP baseline. Times on 256 TPU-v3 cores. Also linear probe, fine-tuning, retrieval and scaling studies.
evidence: "We randomly mask out a large portion (e.g., 50% or 75%) of patches; the ViT encoder is only applied to the visible patches, following [29]" (3. Method); "By default, we apply our models on intact images at inference-time, similar to [29]" (4.1)

name: A-CLIP
main_result: ViT-B/16 on YFCC-15M: ImageNet zero-shot 43.9 at 1.16x CLIP training time (CLIP 37.6 at 1.00x); A-CLIP-eff 42.9 at 0.86x
notes: [vlm?] Token removal only during CLIP pre-training; evaluation uses full images. Each of k=2 masked views keeps 50% of the image tokens (N/k), chosen by [CLS]-to-patch attention averaged over all layers and heads of an EMA copy of the vision encoder run on the full image; the low-score tokens are discarded. The text is not used to score tokens directly; the motivation is that [CLS] attention of a CLIP encoder reflects text-related semantics. Adds online-to-EMA (BYOL) and online-to-online (SimCLR/SimSiam) losses. Training time and memory are relative to CLIP on the same device.
evidence: "we use the attention weights of the [CLS] token of the visual encoder as the correlation scores" (1. Introduction); "In the experiments, the “low” strategy performs best, and is set as the default in our method" (3.3); "In the experiments, k = 2, 3 perform best (see Table 5), and k = 2 is set as default" (3.4)

name: MonoATT
main_result: GUPNet (DLA34) + MonoATT: KITTI test car AP3D (moderate) 17.37 at 56 ms (GUPNet 14.20 at 40 ms)
notes: [application] Monocular 3D detection on KITTI with token clustering inside a transformer on top of a CNN detector. Tokens are the pixels of a DLA34 feature map; a scoring network (depth prior from the camera model plus a learned semantic keypoint heatmap, focal-loss supervised) picks n_l cluster centers per stage, other tokens join the nearest center by feature distance minus pixel distance, and are merged by attention-weighted averaging. Multi-stage feature reconstruction copies merged features back to a full feature map for the detection head. The number of centers per stage is preset. The paper does not say whether the detector starts from pre-trained weights, so training is ?. Time per image is given without batch size or GPU in the text. No code link ("will be released").
evidence: "we first use prior knowledge to design a scoring network for selecting the most important areas of the image, and then propose a token clustering and merging network with an attention mechanism to gradually merge tokens around the selected areas in multiple stages" (Abstract); "The detection network is supervised by LCCE and can be trained jointly with other Mono3D branches" (3.1); "In the upsampling process, we use the record to copy the merged token features to the corresponding upsampled tokens" (3.3)

name: LGViT
main_result: DeiT-B (distilled): ImageNet top-1 81.7 at 10.90 GMACs, 1.67x speed-up (baseline 83.4 at 16.93 GMACs)
notes: [out-of-scope?] Per-image early exit: the whole image leaves at an internal classifier when its confidence exceeds a threshold, and no tokens are removed inside a layer. Local perception heads (convolution) at the lower half and global aggregation heads (pooled self-attention) at the upper half of exit points spaced by equal MACs. Two-stage training: end-to-end fine-tuning of backbone and final classifier, then exit heads trained by self-distillation with the backbone frozen; 100 epochs on 3 RTX 3090. Speed-up is the layer ratio of Eq. 17 and cost is average MACs, not wall-clock. The text names ViT-L/16 as the original ViT model, but Table 1 lists ViT-B/16 (86 M). Also CIFAR-100 and Food-101. No code link in the paper.
evidence: "In the inference stage, each input sample dynamically adjusts its exiting path according to the prediction confidence" (Figure 3); "In the second stage, we froze the parameters of backbone and solely update the exiting heads" (1 Introduction); "Each network is fine-tuned by 100 epochs on 3 NVIDIA 3090 GPUs, with a batch size of 64" (Implementation details)

name: DTMFormer
main_result: SETR + DTMFormer: ACDC Dice 89.64 at 9.8 GFLOPs (SETR 88.56 at 53.2 GFLOPs)
notes: [application] Medical image segmentation (ACDC, ISIC, BTCV) with a plug-in token-merging transformer block. ATM picks the top rN center tokens by a dependence score (column sums of the attention map over half of the heads, with an L1 loss against ground truth) plus a DPC-KNN density-distance feature score; other tokens join centers by feature similarity and are merged with learned weights. LTR copies merged features back to the original token resolution. Sparsity ratio r is a fixed hyper-parameter (ablated 1/2 to 1/32). Networks are trained 400-600 epochs; the paper does not say whether transformer weights start from pre-training, so training is ?. Main goal is accuracy (attention collapse); GFLOPs only, no latency.
evidence: "DTMFormer consists of an attention-guided token merging (ATM) module to adaptively cluster tokens into fewer semantic tokens based on feature and dependency similarity and a light token reconstruction module to fuse ordinary and semantic tokens" (Abstract); "the top rN tokens (i.e., r is the sparsity ratio) with the highest scores are selected as center/semantic tokens for merging" (3.2); "LTR up-samples the token and recovers the feature mapping based on its merging history" (3.3)

name: SparseFormer
main_result: SparseFormer-T: top-1 81.0 at 2.0 GFLOPs, 1270 img/s (Swin-T 81.3 at 4.5 GFLOPs, 726 img/s)
notes: [core] New architecture that represents an image by a small fixed set of latent tokens (49 to 81) with learnable RoIs instead of dense patches. A light focusing transformer adjusts token RoIs and samples features by bilinear interpolation from an early conv feature map; a standard cortex transformer then runs on the latent tokens only. Token count is fixed per variant. Trained from scratch on ImageNet-1k; throughput on one V100 (batch size not in the text). Also Kinetics-400. Not token reduction in a pre-trained ViT. Read the arXiv v1 (only version).
evidence: "SparseFormer learns to represent images using a highly limited number of tokens (down to 49) in the latent space with sparse feature sampling procedure instead of processing dense units in the original pixel space" (Abstract); "SparseFormer uses a learnable linear layer to generate a set of sampling offsets for a token conditionally on its embedding t" (3.1); "SparseFormer, as a new visual architecture, learns to represent an image with sparse tokens from scratch" (3. SparseFormer)

name: Bootstrapped SparseFormer
backbones: AugReg ViT-B/16-224; AugReg ViT-L/16-224; AugReg ViT-L/16-384; CLIP ViT-B/16; CLIP ViT-L/14; CLIP ViT-L/14-336
main_result: AugReg ViT-B/16 to SF-B with 49 tokens: top-1 82.5 at 3.8 GFLOPs, 3001 img/s (ViT-B/16 84.6 at 17.5 GFLOPs, 1126 img/s)
notes: [core] Converts a pre-trained ViT into a SparseFormer with 1/4 of its tokens (49 by default) and reports ImageNet accuracy and throughput. The cortex transformer inherits the ViT blocks (first 1/3 dropped, middle blocks tuned, last 1/3 frozen), a new focusing transformer is trained from random, and the final representation is aligned to the original ViT on ImageNet-1k images without labels. Also CLIP zero-shot and retrieval, MLLM (ScienceQA) and ADE20K segmentation. Throughput on one A5000, fp16, batch 128. Bootstrapping from ViT-L/16 takes 6 hours on 8 A5000.
evidence: "we only need to train the SparseFormer-specific lightweight focusing transformer to adjust token RoIs and fine-tune a few early pre-trained blocks to align the final token representation" (Abstract); "We typically set the number of sparse latent tokens in SparseFormers to 1/4 those in vision transformers" (Figure 2)

name: MoNE
backbones: ViT-S/16; ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16 (ImageNet-21k); ViViT-FE B/16 (Kinetics-400, SSv2)
main_result: ViViT-FE B/16: SSv2 top-1 64.6 at 162.8 GFLOPs (baseline 64.4 at 376.3 GFLOPs)
notes: [out-of-scope?] Tokens are never removed: a router sends each token to one of E nested experts (channel slices of the same weights), so redundant tokens get cheaper computation and the sequence length stays the same. Expert Preferred Routing assigns floor(c_j N) tokens to expert j from the largest expert down; the capacity distribution c is solved with SLSQP from an effective capacity that matches the FLOP budget. Image models are trained from random initialization (AugReg recipe, ImageNet-21k, precision@1); video models start from a pre-trained MatViT and are fine-tuned with isoFLOPs training. FLOPs only; no wall-clock numbers and no code link in the text. Read the arXiv v2 (preprint) version.
evidence: "Given a compute budget, MoNE learns to dynamically choose tokens in a priority order, and thus redundant tokens are processed through cheaper nested experts" (Abstract); "In contrast, our approach does not drop tokens, rather processes them with smaller nested models" (2 Related Work); "For image classification, we train the network with random initialization" (5, Implementation details)

name: ToC3D
backbones: ViT-B (SAM weights); ViT-L (EVA-02 weights); StreamPETR detector
main_result: ViT-B: nuScenes val NDS 55.2 with backbone time 70.3 ms (StreamPETR 55.4 at 85.2 ms), RTX 3090
notes: [application] Multi-view 3D detection on nuScenes with StreamPETR. In 3 blocks MQTS scores image tokens by attention to the top-N_q history object queries (with motion), followed by a linear layer and sigmoid, supervised by projected ground-truth boxes. The top rho N tokens go through the regular blocks with one score-weighted bridge token of the redundant tokens; redundant tokens take the identity path and receive the updated bridge token, so they stay in the sequence. Keep ratios (0.7, 0.5, 0.5) for Fast and (0.5, 0.4, 0.3) for Faster. Trained 24 epochs from SAM / EVA-02 weights. Inference time on one RTX 3090; batch size not stated.
evidence: "MQTS takes image tokens and history object queries as inputs, models the motion information of object queries, and calculates the importance score of each image token through the attention mechanism" (1 Introduction); "ρ is the pre-set constant keeping ratio of each block" (3.2); "we use more neural layers (i.e., regular path) to extract rich semantic and geometric information in salient tokens, while using shallow layers (i.e., free path, we use the identity layer in this paper) to keep the information in redundant tokens" (3.3)

name: TORE
main_result: ViT-B: SUN360 accuracy 74.1 at 7.0 GFLOPs with kappa=8 (AME with ViT-B 64.3 at 38.8 GFLOPs)
notes: [out-of-scope?] Active visual exploration where the saving comes from caching and reusing tokens of earlier glimpses, not from dropping tokens. The ViT is split into an extractor (first kappa blocks) that runs once per glimpse and caches its output tokens, and an aggregator that runs on the union of cached tokens. Glimpses of 2x2 tokens (about 25% of the image in total) are chosen by the attention-map-entropy (AME) policy of a 1-block decoder. kappa is sampled at random during training so one model serves any kappa. ViT-B initialized from MAE weights, trained up to 100 epochs. Also reconstruction. GFLOPs only.
evidence: "It divides the encoder into extractor and aggregator components. The extractor processes each observation separately, enabling the reuse of tokens passed to the aggregator" (Abstract); "The model is initialized with MAE [8] weights pretrained on ImageNet-1k [4]" (4.1)

name: Patch Ranking
main_result: CLIP ViT-B/16: zero-shot average over 8 datasets 66.3 at 16.8 GFLOPs (full model 67.9 at 23.4); with text+visual prompt tuning 79.5 at 20.9 (79.8 at 27.6)
notes: [vlm?] Token pruning in the CLIP image encoder, evaluated by zero-shot and 16-shot classification. A Golden Ranking of patch tokens is built offline by greedy search with one of three scores, and a one-layer Mix-MLP predictor on early-layer features is trained to regress it; at inference 20 tokens are removed at each of layers 4, 6, 8, 10 (40% removed). CLIP is not fine-tuned: only the predictor and optional learnable text and visual prompt tokens (16 shots per class) are trained. GFLOPs and time per image (1.6 vs 3.5 ms at 60% keep rate) on an NVIDIA A4500; batch size not stated.
evidence: "we propose greedy search methods to establish a “Golden Ranking” and introduce a lightweight predictor specifically trained to approximate this Ranking" (Abstract); "Instead, inspired by prompt-tuning strategies [12, 33], we introduce a set of learnable tokens into the CLIP model and train them using a small dataset to compensate for the performance degradation" (3.3); "Pruning occurs progressively at the 4th, 6th, 8th, and 10th layers, removing 20 tokens each" (Table 5)

name: ImagePiece
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 80.22 at 3891.9 img/s (DeiT-S 79.83 at 2531.1 img/s)
notes: [core] Token merging plus pruning for DeiT on ImageNet-1k. The bottom 30% tokens by [CLS] attention are split into two sets and merged by bipartite soft matching (0.08 x tokens per step); their [CLS] attention is then recomputed and the bottom 20% are discarded (keep 0.8). A conv stem (four 3x3 and one 1x1 conv) replaces the patchify stem, and models are trained from scratch for 300 epochs with the DeiT recipe, so the DeiT-S numbers are for a modified DeiT-S. Throughput on one RTX 3090; no FLOPs, batch size or code link in the paper.
evidence: "ImagePiece groups semantically insufficient (bottom-k) tokens to a level that convey meaning" (Introduction); "each token in group A is merged with the most similar token in group B using bipartite soft matching (Bolya et al. 2023)" (ImagePiece); "We train our model from scratch for 300 epochs" (Implementation details); "we set the pruning ratio r to 0.8, which results in discarding the bottom 20% of tokens" (Implementation details)

name: CLCA
backbones: ViT-B/16 pre-trained as ViT, DeiT, DeiT3 (IN-1k and IN-21k), MIIL, MoCo v3, DINO, MAE, CLIP (LAION)
main_result: CLCA with EViT at 10% keep rate: SoyAgeing top-1 87.4 at 25.2 GFLOPs (ViT 67.0 at 78.5 GFLOPs)
notes: [application] Ultra-fine-grained leaf cultivar recognition (5 datasets) with an add-on for existing token reduction. Reduction is mainly EViT (top-k by [CLS] attention, rest fused into one token; also DynamicViT, ATS, SiT, PatchMerger, DPC-KNN, ToMe) at layers 4, 7, 10 of ViT-B/16. A Cross-Layer Cache stores GAP features and a register token after each block and appends them back after each reduction, and a Cross-Layer Aggregation head classifies from the CLS outputs of all groups. Keep rates 100 to 10%. Pre-trained backbones fine-tuned 50 epochs at image size 224 or 448. Table I does not say which backbone the CLCA rows use. FLOPs only.
evidence: "Our method can be combined with most token reduction methodologies but we focus on EViT [15]" (III.A); "After the reduction location or before the last layer, we access the CLC to recover the lost information tokens by appending the tokens stored in it to the original sequence" (III.C); "We employ AdamW optimizer, 50 epochs, weight decay of 0.05, batch size of 32, two image sizes (224, 448), nine backbones" (IV)
